body:
Even though `Math.Abs` has both a `float` and `double` overload, most methods in `Math` only take `double`. That's why in the Vector types we use `Mathf` everywhere, to ensure both overloads exist and it will work for `real_t` regardless of whether it's `float` or `double`.

```suggestion
            n /= Mathf.Abs(n.X) + Mathf.Abs(n.Y) + Mathf.Abs(n.Z);
```
Ah gotcha. For some reason I thought the other calls were to `System.MathF` rather than `Godot.Mathf` 🤦
